candidates.source_title: Man, 52, dies after 'incident' in Rochdale, sparking murder investigation
candidates.source_summary: Two men are in custody.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: There was an ‘incident’ on South Parade in Rochdale (Picture: Google Maps) Police have launched a murder investigation following an ‘incident’ in Rochdale, which led to the death of a man. Officers were called out to the town centre at around 1.30am today, where they found the 52-year-old unconscious after he was assaulted on South Parade, between The Old Bank bar and AST Hampsons Solicitors. Greater Manchester Police confirmed that Northwest Ambulance Service and GMP attended the scene. He was taken to hospital for treatment, where, despite the best efforts of emergency services, he died from his injuries. His family members are being supported by specialist officers. Two men are in custody and are being questioned in connection with the incident. The police are appealing for any witnesses or anyone with CCTV or mobile phone footage to come forward to assist with enquiries. Detective Chief Inspector Claire Brennan from the Major Incident Team said: ‘This is a heartbreaking incident in which a man has tragically lost his life. ‘Our thoughts are first and foremost with his family and loved ones who are being supported by specially trained officers at this incredibly difficult time.’ She added: ‘We understand an incident of this nature will also cause concern within the local community. ‘I want to reassure people that we have a dedicated team of detectives working to establish the full circumstances surrounding this incident and understand exactly what happened in the moments leading up to it.’ The investigation is ‘ongoing’, as an appeal has been launched directly to anyone who was in the South Parade area in the small hours on Saturday. Police are keen to hear from those who ‘may have witnessed the incident or seen anything suspicious before or afterwards’. ‘If you have any information, no matter how insignificant you think it may be, please come forward and speak to our officers on 101 or LiveChat, quoting log 250 of 26/09/2026. ‘Alternatively, contact independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.’ Get in touch with our news team by emailing us at webnews@metro.co.uk. For more stories like this, check our news page.

Police said his family were being supported by specialist officers. Det Ch Insp Claire Brennan, whose force has appealed for any CCTV, doorbell or dashcam footage, described what had happened as a "heart-breaking incident". candidates.source_body_excerpt: A murder investigation has been launched after a 52-year-old man died following a reported assault on South Parade in Rochdale early on Saturday 26 September. Two men have been arrested in connection with the incident, Greater Manchester Police said. Officers were called at about 1.30am and found the man unconscious. He was taken to hospital, where he died. Police said his family are being supported by specialist officers. The two arrested men remained in custody for questioning when police issued their update. Detectives from the Major Incident Team are investigating. Detective Chief Inspector Claire Brennan said: “This is a heart-breaking incident in which a man has tragically lost his life. “Our thoughts are first and foremost with his family and loved ones who are being supported by specially trained officers at this incredibly difficult time. “We understand an incident of this nature will also cause concern within the local community. I want to reassure people that we have a dedicated team of detectives working to establish the full circumstances surrounding this incident and understand exactly what happened in the moments leading up to it. “Two men have been arrested in connection with the incident and our enquiries remain ongoing. “We are now appealing directly to anyone who was in the South Parade area in the early hours of this morning and may have witnessed the incident, or seen anything suspicious before or afterwards, to please speak to us.

candidates.source_title: Family pay tribute to 85-year-old woman who died after Leigh collision
candidates.source_summary: The family of an 85-year-old woman who died following a collision in Leigh have paid tribute to her.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The family of an 85-year-old woman who died following a collision in Leigh have paid tribute to her. The collision happened shortly after 4pm on Monday 14 September. Another occupant of the car was injured and remains in hospital in a serious condition, according to Greater Manchester Police. GMP's Serious Collision Investigation Unit is investigating the circumstances. Ethel's family said: “We are heartbroken to announce the passing of our beloved mother, Ethel Walsh, aged 85, following a road traffic collision on 14 September. “Ethel was a dearly loved mother, nana, sister and friend, who brought immense warmth, joy, and kindness to everyone who knew her. She was a gentle, strong, and independent woman who lived a full and contented life, and her sudden loss has left an immeasurable void in our family. “We would like to express our deepest gratitude to the emergency services, the medical team at the Greater Manchester Major Trauma Hospital, and the police family liaison officer for their care and support during this devastating time. “As the police investigation into the circumstances of the collision remains ongoing, we kindly ask for privacy as we grieve and remember the wonderful woman she was.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Originally posted on June 2, 2023 @ 09:15 Health leaders from Rochdale, Greater Manchester, have shared the success of their collaborative working model with more than 1,000 delegates at a conference in Belgium. Dr Salman Shahid, Associate Medical Director of the Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board, along with a team from One Rochdale Health and Care, presented their integrated approach to healthcare, focusing on improving the well-being of individuals in Rochdale and the wider Greater Manchester region at the International Conference on Integrated Care in Antwerp. candidates.source_title: Digital autopsies to help reduce distress of post-mortems - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Pioneering digital autopsies could cut the need for invasive post-mortems by up to 80 per cent, reducing the distress caused to grieving loved ones.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Pioneering digital autopsies could cut the need for invasive post-mortems by up to 80 per cent, reducing the distress caused to grieving loved ones. The innovative service is being delivered by the Coroner’s Office for Greater Manchester, in partnership with the NHS, specialist post-mortem imaging provider Anubix, and medical imaging provider TIC Health. Working with pathologists, radiologists and mortuary staff at the Northern Care Alliance the coroner’s office will, where appropriate, provide computed tomography (CT) scanning to help inform a person’s cause of death. Teams will use post-mortem imaging to check if a cause of death can be determined without the need for traditional invasive post-mortems, a process that can cause further distress to relatives during the grieving process across Rochdale, Bury, and Oldham. A number of scans a week will be carried out using the new technology, with a long-term ambition of speeding up the service provided for relatives following the loss of a loved one. Cllr Neil Emmott, leader of Rochdale Council, said: “This is a highly sensitive issue that has been carefully handled. “Working in partnership across the health sector, this will help to futureproof the coroner’s service and ensure families and loved ones continue to get the best possible support. “I know from speaking with residents across Heywood, Middleton, Pennines and Rochdale how invasive post-mortems often causes additional anxiety at a time of grief, so this is a timely and welcome new service.”

The innovative service is being delivered by the Coroner’s Office for Greater Manchester, in partnership with the NHS, specialist post-mortem imaging provider Anubix, and medical imaging provider TIC Health. Working with pathologists, radiologists and mortuary staff at the Northern Care Alliance the coroner’s office will, where appropriate, provide computed tomography (CT) scanning to help inform a person’s cause of death. Teams will use post-mortem imaging to check if a cause of death can be determined without the need for traditional invasive post-mortems, a process that can cause further distress to relatives during the grieving process. A number of scans a week will be carried out using the new technology, with a long-term ambition of speeding up the service provided for relatives following the loss of a loved one. Councillor Neil Emmott, leader of Rochdale Borough Council, said: “This is a highly sensitive issue that has been carefully handled. Working in partnership across the health sector, this will help to futureproof the coroner’s service and ensure families and loved ones continue to get the best possible support. candidates.source_body_excerpt: The kick pitch is located by The Burnside Centre in Middleton. Residents in Middleton are campaigning for a replacement football pitch after plans were announced to turn the existing site into a car park. Campaigners say the pitch in Burnside Crescent on the Langley Estate is a community hub as well as somewhere people can play football and other sports. The pitch, which is next to the Burnside Centre, is one of three on the estate, and the car park will be for the centre. Families say they have been told replacement facilities will be provided at Rochdale AFC and Rochdale Council's planned Football and Community Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee Playing Fields. But they are campaigning for the new pitch to be created on land next to the original. The Burnside Centre said it understands why people are disappointed to see the pitch decommissioned, but said one of the reasons the decision was made related to concerns about antisocial behaviour. It added: "The pitch, which dates back to the late 1990s, had reached the end of its expected lifespan and required significant investment to remain operational." Resident Kelly Burton has four children, three of whom use the football pitch regularly.

Jamie Dale, 47, from Rochdale, in Greater Manchester, spent more than 11 years in prison for his involvement in organised crime. He now runs the Old Lags Network, which aims to cut reoffending and bridge the gap between prison and the community. He said many prisoners "fall through the cracks" after release. "Most of the people who return quite quickly have not got great family networks," he said. Dale set up the Old Lags Network in September 2025 to provide support to prison leavers Dale said involving ex-offenders in developing solutions would "drastically reduce the amount of people being recalled to prison". candidates.source_body_excerpt: Will Place, seen here with his mother Beverley, died when he crashed his car after drinking while watching an England match An inquest jury has found that a man died after drink-driving at speeds of more than 70mph before he crashed into a pub in Heywood, Greater Manchester. Will Place, 23, had been drinking in Rochdale after watching the England vs Slovakia match at Euro 2024 and got behind the wheel of his car in the early hours of Monday 1st July 2024. When police in a marked van saw him pass a red light on Manchester Road, they immediately began following him at high speed - but officers called off the pursuit shortly before Mr Place collided into the White Lion pub. The narrative verdict made no mention about the conduct of police officers who had responded to the incident in the moments before the fatal crash. The inquest jury at Rochdale Coroner's Court found that, on the balance of probabilities, alcohol played a contributing factor to Place's decision-making in the moments before he died. In their verdict, the jury also found that his speed was excessive throughout the pursuit and a bend in the road contributed to the instability of the vehicle. A post-mortem examination following the crash found that Place had suffered catastrophic injuries and he was twice the legal limit for drink-driving.

This October, Rochdale residents have a rewarding new reason to lace up their walking boots and step outdoors. The charity Hearing Dogs for Deaf People is inviting the local community to explore the town’s scenic trails, historic landmarks, and hidden gems on foot- all while raising vital funds to transform the lives of deaf people across the region. The autumn initiative, known as the Great British Dog Walk, challenges participants to clock up a total of 70 miles throughout the month. Supported by the charity’s active puppy training hub based right in Rochdale, the campaign encourages walkers of all ages and abilities to discover new corner-of-the-map adventures or simply add extra distance to their favourite everyday routes. Every step taken carries a powerful meaning behind the mileage. The 70-mile target symbolises the average £70,000 lifetime cost to train and support a single, life-changing hearing dog. By turning routine strolls into sponsored miles, local participants will directly help fund the careful breeding, puppy socialisation, and specialised training required to match these remarkable dogs with those who need them most.
